docs.title: ServiceMesh Benchmarl: The Workshop
docs.text:
This environment will deploy the Booking app with a one of the Service Mesh covered by the Benchmark. It will send Metrics , logs and traces to Dynatrace

  • Click Here to Begin

docs.title: 4. Cleanup
docs.text:
Run in CloudRun Locally

To cleanup resources, go to https://github.com/codespaces and delete the codespace.

  1. In the original VSCode window, go to the "Remote Explorer" panel (down the left hand side)

  2. Expand the "Dev Containers" category, hover over the obslab-k6 container and click the X to delete

You may also want to deactivate or delete the API token.

docs.title: Gather Details: Tenant ID & Environment
docs.text:
You will need access to a Dynatrace tenant. If you do not have access, sign up for a free 15 day trial.

Make a note of your Dynatrace tenant ID. It is the first bit of your URL (eg. abc12345 in the following examples):

https://abc12345.live.dynatrace.com
https://abc12345.apps.dynatrace.com

docs.title: Gather Details: Environment Type
docs.text:
Make a note of your "environment type" based on your URL.

If you are unsure, use live.

URL Environment Type abc12345.apps.dynatrace.com live abc12345.live.dynatrace.com live abc12345.sprint.dynatracelabs.com sprint abc12345.dev.dynatracelabs.com dev

docs.title: Gather Details: Create API Token
docs.text: This Workshop requires an 2 API tokens: * One to deploy the Dynatrace Operator * One to ingest metrics, logs, traces and events

docs.title: Operator token  permissions:
docs.text:
• Create ActiveGate tokens
  • Read entities
  • Read Settings
  • Write Settings
  • Access problem and event feed, metrics and topology
  • Read configuration
  • Write configuration
  • Paas integration - installer downloader

docs.title: Ingest token permissions :
docs.text:
• Ingest metrics (metrics.ingest)
  • Ingest logs (logs.ingest)
  • Ingest events (events.ingest)
  • Ingest OpenTelemetry
  • Read metrics

The codspace will require to define several details: 

* Environment ID
* Environment Type
* Operator API Token
* Ingest API Token
* Service Mesh Type
* Cluster Name

docs.title: Start Demo
docs.text:
Run in CloudRun Locally

Click this button to launch the demo in a new tab.

  • Clone the repository to your local machine

    git clone https://github.com/isItObservable/servicemeshsecuritybenchmark.git
    • Open the folder in Visual Studio code
    • Ensure the Microsoft Dev Containers extension and Dev Containers CLI are installed in VSCode
    • Open a new terminal in VSCode and set your environment variables as appropriate:
    set DT_ENVIRONMENT_ID=abc12345
set DT_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE=live
set DT_API_TOKEN=dt0c01.******.***********
set DT_OPERATOR_TOKEN=dt0c01.******.***********
set SM_TYPE=istio ( value could be equal to : kuma, linkerd, istio, ambient, ambient-kgateway
set NAME= <Name of your environment
    • Start Docker / Podman
    • Create the environment
    devcontainer up

    It will take a few moments but you should see:

    {"outcome":"success","containerId":"...","remoteUser":"root","remoteWorkspaceFolder":"/workspaces/servicemeshsecuritybenchmark"}
    • Connect to the demo environment. This will launch a new Visual Studio Code window 
      devcontainer open

    In the new Visual Studio code window, open a new terminal and continue with the tutorial.

  • Click Here to Run the Demo

docs.title: Servicemesh type
docs.text:
This Workshop Covers the support of: * Kuma * Linkerd with the Kgateway * Istio * Ambient Mesh * Ambient Mesh with the Kgateway

The purpose is to define which service mesh you would like to try . This would be done by setting the right value to SM_TYPE. The current value supported are: - none: meaning that no service mesh would be deployed - linkerd - istio - ambient - ambient-kgateway
